name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,794

entries.clue: Suffolk town known for trawling, not frequently right at the bottom (6)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not frequently' tells you to take the word for frequently out

blocks.note: Lowestoft is a fishing port on the Suffolk coast in eastern England
oft = often, frequently; removed from the end

annotation.surface: A travel-guide line about an English fishing town and how often its boats go out.
annotation.walkthrough: The town is clued by description, not name, so you need to know Lowestoft, England's most easterly town, famous for its fishing fleet.
annotation.definitionFit: Something right at the bottom of a list or scale is the lowest.

entries.clue: City's providing support for toilets, just about (7)

indicatorNotes.providing support for: in a down entry, the thing giving support sits underneath, so the city goes below the toilets

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

annotation.surface: A council boasting that the city pays for its public toilets, more or less.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Providing support for' only works in a down clue: ELY is written under LOOS, holding it up.
annotation.definitionFit: Loosely translated means translated just about, roughly rather than exactly.

entries.clue: Crucial point in arrangement of draw-sheet (9)

indicatorNotes.arrangement of: an arrangement of letters is a rearranging of them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A nursing note about the key moment in making up a hospital bed with a draw-sheet.
annotation.walkthrough: A draw-sheet is a narrow sheet laid across a hospital bed; its hyphen is ignored, leaving exactly the nine letters needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A watershed is a turning point, a moment after which things are different.

entries.clue: Son's missing out on love with long nose (6)

indicatorNotes.missing out: 'on' missing out 'love' means O is left out of ON

blocks.note: s = son, as in genealogies
ON without O (love, the zero in tennis scoring) leaves N
to long for something is to itch for it

annotation.surface: A son missing out on romance because of his long nose, a Cyrano-like complaint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long nose' looks like a single phrase; split it, and 'long' is the verb giving ITCH while 'nose' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Snitch is old slang for the nose, and a nose is also a police informer, which a snitch is too.

entries.clue: Party finishing early had perplexed Nirvana fan (6)

indicatorNotes.finishing early: the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: SIDE (a party in a dispute) loses its final E
HAD rearranged

annotation.surface: A party breaking up early because a Nirvana fan was confused, as if the grunge band were playing.
annotation.walkthrough: Nirvana here is not the rock band but the state of spiritual liberation; a siddha is someone who has reached it.
annotation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Jain belief a siddha is a perfected being who has attained liberation, so a devotee of nirvana.

entries.clue: Swallowed in-joke on the podcast edition (8)

indicatorNotes.on the podcast: a podcast is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the first part of 'in-joke' taken as it stands
a jest is a joke; GEST sounds the same
ed. = edition

annotation.surface: A podcast edition in which an in-joke went down badly.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'in-joke' has to be split into IN and JOKE; 'Swallowed' at the front looks like a verb in the story but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ingested means taken in as food: swallowed.

entries.clue: Put off by man not closing washing up liquid? (5)

indicatorNotes.not closing: the man is not at the close, the end of the word, any more

blocks.note: washing-up liquid is an example of a detergent, hence the question mark
gent = gentleman, man; removed from the end

annotation.surface: Someone discouraged by a man who never finishes the washing-up.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: washing-up liquid is one kind of detergent.
annotation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off doing something.

entries.clue: Dropping off a sack full of money (7)

indicatorNotes.full of: the sack is full of, holds, the money

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a sack is a bag; it goes round the money
tin is old British slang for money

annotation.surface: A robber losing grip of a bag stuffed with cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' suggests falling asleep or delivering; here it means declining, as a wind or a fever does. Tin is old British slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: A storm that is abating is dropping off, lessening in strength.

entries.clue: Businessmen represent and run European supply (13)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as 'supple-y', in a supple, bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram fodder, 3 letters
E = European

annotation.surface: A trade body's mission: businessmen who stand for and manage European supply chains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun about goods; it is the adverb of supple, telling you to bend the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Entrepreneurs are people who start and run businesses.

entries.clue: Rebellious type without his trousers (6)

indicatorNotes.trousers: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words pocket the answer

blocks.note: witHOUT HIs

annotation.surface: A rebel caught without his trousers, a comic scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb, not clothing: the phrase 'without his' trousers (pockets) the answer. The Houthis are a rebel movement in Yemen.
annotation.definitionFit: A Houthi is a member of the Yemeni rebel movement, so a rebellious type.

entries.clue: Patching damaged item of sleepwear (8)

indicatorNotes.damaged: damaged letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Mending a torn piece of nightwear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is so domestic that 'Patching damaged' reads as a single action, hiding the fact that 'Patching' is the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a soft cap once worn in bed.

entries.clue: Express disapproval when trust is often lacking (3)

indicatorNotes.often lacking: letters are lacking at frequent, regular intervals, so every other one goes

blocks.note: keep the first, third and fifth letters of the word

annotation.surface: A sigh of disapproval at how rarely people trust each other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Often lacking' sounds like a comment on society; it tells you to drop every second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The word imitates the tongue-click people make when displeased, and it is also used as a verb for making it.

entries.clue: Irony as mistake by international stops Manchester City? (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the mistake goes inside

blocks.note: Manchester City FC, the football club; it goes round the rest
to err is to make a mistake
I = international

annotation.surface: A sports report on the irony of an international player's blunder halting Manchester City.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irony' is not sarcasm but the adjective 'iron-y', made of iron. FC stands for Football Club, the suffix of Manchester City.
annotation.definitionFit: Ferric means containing iron, so iron-like: irony.

entries.clue: Check riddle again? (8)

blocks.note: re- = again, as in redo
to riddle is to sieve, to strain

annotation.surface: A puzzle-setter asking to look at a riddle once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is not a puzzle but a coarse sieve; 'Check' looks like a request but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to restrain it, hold it back.

entries.clue: Maya, the missing vowels legend! (4)

blocks.note: MAYA without its A's
THE without its E

annotation.surface: A fan hailing a woman called Maya as a legend, even without her vowels.
annotation.walkthrough: Maya, a name and the Mayan civilisation, feels like it should be the legend; it is just letters to strip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are traditional stories handed down, not to be taken as fact.

entries.clue: A very quiet final period for the tail? (9)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
pp = pianissimo, very quiet in music
the end is the final part
an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A wry question whether a tail's last stretch is a very quiet time.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a tail is one kind of appendage.
annotation.definitionFit: A tail is an appendage, a part attached to the main body.

entries.clue: Number 23's opposite is a plant (9)

blocks.note: 23 across is ANALOGUE, whose opposite is DIGITAL
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A botanical riddle: the flip side of some numbered thing turns out to be a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number 23' points to the answer at 23 across; 'Number' also hints at digits, the root of DIGITAL.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the botanical genus of the foxglove, and also names the heart drug made from its leaves.

entries.clue: Family goes on vacation to North London borough (8)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: your kin are your family
GOES emptied of its middle
taken as it stands
N = North

annotation.surface: A family heading off on holiday to a borough in north London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North London borough' reads as one phrase, but North is N and the definition is just 'London borough': Kingston upon Thames is in south-west London.
annotation.definitionFit: Kingston upon Thames is one of the London boroughs.

entries.clue: Spooner produces anti-depressant from this kitchen appliance (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Spooner produces: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version swaps them

blocks.note: a mood fixer lifts depression; swap the M and F

annotation.surface: A claim that Dr Spooner could make a happy pill out of a kitchen gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: The anti-depressant is described, not named: something that fixes your mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A food mixer is an electric kitchen appliance for beating and mixing.

entries.clue: Topless dress design is self-inflicted disaster (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Topless: the word loses its top, the first letter in a down clue

blocks.note: GOWN without its G
a design is an aim, a goal

annotation.surface: A fashion commentator calling a topless dress design a disaster of the designer's own making.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Design' looks like a noun about fashion; it is the sense of purpose, as in 'by design'.
annotation.definitionFit: An own goal, scoring into your own net, is any self-inflicted setback.

entries.clue: Silverback training to open mouth wide (4)

indicatorNotes.back: the silver comes back, reading right to left

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, then read back
PE = physical education

annotation.surface: A gorilla being trained to open its mouth wide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silverback' is one word for a male gorilla, which points at APE; split it into Silver and back instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for the open-mouthed stare of astonishment.

entries.clue: Address of on-line retailer that is into up-cycling is much-visited site (7)

indicatorNotes.into: the address and 'that is' go into the other piece
indicatorNotes.up-cycling: UP cycled, turned over, in a down clue reads upward: PU

blocks.note: taken as it stands, then turned over to PU
a URL is a web address
i.e. = id est, that is

annotation.surface: A trendy online upcycling shop with a very busy website.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up-cycling' is a trendy word for reusing old things; split it so 'up' is the letters and 'cycling' turns them round.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone's purlieus are their haunts, the places they often visit.

entries.clue: Oddly, skivers are claiming time for afternoon nap! (6)

indicatorNotes.claiming: the letters claim, take hold of, the time

blocks.note: S_I_E_S: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
an are is a metric unit of area, a
t = time; claimed between SIES and A

annotation.surface: Workshy staff insisting they need time for an afternoon nap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb but is a noun: the metric unit of area, abbreviated a.
annotation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, taken in hot countries.

entries.clue: 19 Brussels bureaucrats held back after obsessive type of display? (8)

indicatorNotes.held back: the bureaucrats are held in reverse, reading right to left
indicatorNotes.after: the rest comes after the obsessive piece

blocks.note: anal = obsessively fussy
19 down is OWN GOAL, abbreviated OG
the European Union, based in Brussels

annotation.surface: Nineteen Brussels officials delayed because of someone fussy about a display.
annotation.walkthrough: '19' is a cross-reference to 19 down, OWN GOAL, used here in its abbreviation OG.
annotation.definitionFit: An analogue display, such as a clock face with hands, shows values continuously rather than as digits.

entries.clue: Artist originally rejected slow track (5)

indicatorNotes.originally rejected: the original, first, letter is rejected

blocks.note: SLOW without its first letter
Ry = railway, a track

annotation.surface: An artist's work turned down at first, sent down a slow track.
annotation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial towns and their 'matchstick' figures.
annotation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry is a well-known English artist.

entries.clue: Person training in the arena regularly (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: taken as it stands
T_E_R_N: the odd letters of THEARENA

annotation.surface: An athlete regularly working out in the arena.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Training' in the surface suggests sport; the definition is a trainee in a job.
annotation.definitionFit: An intern is a trainee gaining work experience, a person in training.

entries.clue: Custom house centrally located next to sea after docking (3)

indicatorNotes.centrally located: only the central letter is used
indicatorNotes.after docking: docking a tail cuts it short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the middle letter of HOUSE
SEA without its last letter

annotation.surface: A customs house on the quay, beside the sea where ships dock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Custom house' is a real building at a port, and 'docking' fits ships; split off Custom as the definition and read docking as trimming.
annotation.definitionFit: Use, as in 'use and custom', means established practice or habit.

entries.clue: Two suffering with heart trouble (3,5)

indicatorNotes.suffering: suffering letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 3 letters
anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: Two patients with heart problems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heart trouble' reads as one medical phrase; 'heart' is fodder and 'trouble' alone is the definition, used as in 'in hot water'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone in a scrape is said to be 'in hot water', so the phrase stands for trouble.

entries.clue: One captured is held at arm’s length? (6)

annotation.definition: One captured is held at arm’s length?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a prisoner taken and kept
the meant reading: a phone camera held out at arm's length to photograph yourself

annotation.surface: Someone taken prisoner and kept at a distance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captured' suggests a prisoner, and 'held at arm's length' suggests being kept away; both describe a photo taken with the phone at arm's length.
annotation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photo captured with the camera held at arm's length.

entries.clue: Egg production is spreading (6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Egg production' is a noun phrase; LAYING works as the noun, as in 'the hens' laying'.

blocks.note: what hens do to produce eggs
as when a carpet or tablecloth is spread out flat

annotation.surface: A farm fact: egg production is expanding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' as in laying a carpet or laying a table, putting something down flat.
annotation.definitionFit: Hens laying produce eggs, and laying a carpet spreads it over the floor.

entries.clue: North America succeeded, primarily swapping gold for capital in the Caribbean (6)

blocks.note: the initials of North America
s. = succeeded, as in family trees
the first letter of SWAPPING
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: A trade report: North America did well by trading its gold for Caribbean money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swapping gold for capital' reads as a trade; 'for' only links, and 'capital' is the city.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the capital of the Bahamas, which are loosely counted as part of the Caribbean.
